rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi adopts the muṣḥaf reading, finding no need to force an interpretation because context and Qur’anic parallels yield a clear reading; variant readings would revive doubts removed by Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: At no place did I need to artificially adjust an interpretation; at all places a very clear and lucid interpretation in the light of the context and parallels of the Qur’ ān came to surface

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects identifying the seven aḥruf with seven readings; taking ḥarf as writing, discourse, or style makes the report refer to the Qur’an’s seven discernible groups.
rows.anchor: if the word ḥarf (singular of aḥruf) is interpreted as “a writing, a discourse or a style,” which has full sanction from lexicons as well as usage

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each of the seven groups gathers the Qur’anic message under a central theme, varying style and argument so repetition stays fresh and new in flavor.
rows.anchor: under a comprehensive central theme, all the basic meanings of the Qur’ ānic preaching are mentioned in various styles in such a manner that, in spite of repetition, a reader does not feel tired of the discourse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The groups together constitute the great Qur’an referenced in 15:87; the particle wāw there is explanatory.
rows.anchor: the great Qur’ān, (15:87)) mentioned in Sūrah al-Ḥijr. The particle وas I have explained in the exegesis of the sūrah, is for explication.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah’s central theme is warning about both worldly punishment for rejecting a messenger and punishment in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: The central theme of this sūrah is indhār (warning) and this includes indhār regarding both types of punishment: the punishment which the rejecters of a messenger of God face in this world, and the punishment they will have to face in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is argued from signs in the world: observation reveals divine attributes that require the world to reach its culmination.
rows.anchor: The arguments are drawn from the signs of God in the world around man. It has been told in this sūrah that, an observation of this world higlights those attributes of God which necessitate the fact that this world shall one day reach its culmination.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those enslaved to desire who fail to use reason go to Hell, while those who reason and fear God unseen merit great reward.
rows.anchor: People who led their lives while being slaves to their desires and did not use their intellect will be cast into Hell, and those who used their intellect, and feared the Almighty even though they had not seen Him, will become worthy of great reward.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scrutiny of the universe shows that its sovereign is blessed and powerful; life and death have purpose, and the world is a test rather than an endless or abrupt process.
rows.anchor: A close scrutiny of the universe reveals that its sovereign is a Blessed and Powerful Being. He has created life and death with a purpose and it is not that this world is to continue like this forever or suddenly end

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is a trial to distinguish those who take the right path from those who take the wrong one, requiring a Day when the righteous are rewarded and rebels punished.
rows.anchor: adopts the right path and who the wrong one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated observation of the universe’s power and blessings reveals no flaw in its vast expanse.
rows.anchor: not even a minor flaw can be pointed out in its great expanse. Repeated observations will only second this inference.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearest heaven is adorned with stars that guide travelers and repel Satan and his army when they try to overhear revelation.
rows.anchor: The nearest of the seven skies has been adorned with stars by the Almighty; they serve the dual purpose of guiding people in their journeys and pelting Satan and his army if they try to overhear something revealed by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evident divine power and providence show that deniers of the Day of Reward and Punishment will face Hell, which roars and shrieks like a hungry lion.
rows.anchor: The power and providence of the Almighty so evident in this universe bears evidence that those who deny the Day of Reward and Punishment will have to face the torment of Hell. It will roar and shriek like a hungry lion when it sees them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell’s keepers ask each group whether a warner had warned them; they admit a warner came but that they rejected him.
rows.anchor: Whenever a group of these rebellious people will be flung in Hell, its gate-keepers will ask them whether a warner had ever warned them of this punishment. They would admit that a warner did come to them, but they rejected him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned confess they called belief in revelation deviation and failed to listen or understand, bringing about their fate.
rows.anchor: whoever believed that the Almighty has revealed anything have, in fact, deviated from the right path. They would also confess that they had never tried to listen to, and understand what had been said to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear their Lord unseen are promised reward; God knows and repays their virtuous deeds, since nothing is hidden from the Creator who knows all.
rows.anchor: people who remain fearful of their Lord in this world shall be rewarded. They are assured that all their virtuous deeds are in the knowledge of God and He shall duly reward them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is made submissive for human use, but its benefits should remind people of accountability and God’s power to destroy them through calamity.
rows.anchor: this earth has been created by the Almighty and is very obedient and submissive to man. Its creation and existence is a source of reminder for man of a great reality: he should roam about in it and fully benefit from all its pleasures and facilities, but should always keep in mind that these privileges entail a day of accountability before the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything suspended in the skies is held by God, who watches all; without his support no one can help a person, and no one else can provide sustenance if he withholds it.
rows.anchor: whatever is suspended in the unfathomable skies is held by the Almighty. He is watching over everything. If someone is deprived of His assistance and support, no one will be able to help him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God withholds a person’s sustenance, no one can give it to him.
rows.anchor: If He deprives a person of sustenance, no one can grant him sustenance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People enslaved to desire never reach the true goal; only those who stay on the right path do so.
rows.anchor: Those who lead their lives while remaining slaves to their desires will never reach the real goal. Only those who remain on the right path will reach this goal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave people sight, hearing, and reasoning to help them stay on the right path, yet few appreciate these gifts.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has endowed people with the faculties of sight, hearing and reasoning so that people can remain on the right path by using them. But alas! very few people understand the worth of such favours.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God scattered humanity across earth and will gather them; only God knows when Judgment comes, and the Prophet is told to say he does not know its time.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has scattered mankind all over this earth and He Himself shall definitely gather them one day. The Prophet (sws) is told to inform the disbelievers that only God knows when the Day of Judgement will come and that he himself has no

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Takwīr depicts the Judgment’s terror, named ṭāmmah and ṣākhkhah in the preceding ʿAbas and al-Nāziʿāt, affecting the cosmos and the world around and within people.
rows.anchor: This sūrah portrays the horrors of the Day of Judgement mentioned in the previous two sūrahs – ‘Abas and al-N āzi‘ āt – by the names ṭāmmah and ṣākhkhah .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vivid portrayal lets a discerning person see what is now hidden but will later be revealed.
rows.anchor: if a person has a discerning mind he can see all that is today concealed from his eyes but will one day be revealed to him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are urged to heed the Qur’an’s warning and prepare; its source is God and its bearer is the trustworthy, favored angel, not a poet or soothsayer.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ ān is from God and He has revealed it to His Prophet through His most trustworthy and favoured angel.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting the Qur’an as poetry or soothsaying harms neither God nor the Prophet; it brings doom on the rejecters, while the messenger’s duty is to remind.
rows.anchor: they will neither be able to harm God nor His Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those who truly honor truth will be granted the urge to believe in the Book, an unchanging divine practice.
rows.anchor: only those people will be blessed with the urge to profess faith in this Book who truly value and honour the truth. This is an established practice of God and there can be no change in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 1–3 portray what happens to the great things of this world: the sun, moon, and mountains.
rows.anchor: What will befall the great and grand things of this world like the sun, the moon and the mountains is portrayed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 4–6 show every being concerned for itself and cherished things abandoned; terrified wild animals gather near one another as seas become tempestuous.
rows.anchor: The manner in which each and every thing on this earth will only be concerned about its own self is briefly mentione d. The most cherished and favourite of things will be abandoned.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Infiṭār is the counterpart of al-Takwīr, sharing its intrinsic and extrinsic form, style, meanings, and opening cataclysm.
rows.anchor: great similarity between the intrinsic and extrinsic form, style and meanings of both sūrahs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sūrahs express the same outcome in parallel: each soul learns what it sent forward, with al-Infiṭār adding what it left behind.
rows.anchor: The real objective of each of these sūrahs is also mentioned in very similar words.

rows.speaker: scholars of the past
rows.claim: Earlier scholars said readers wanting a picture of Judgment’s upheaval should read al-Takwīr and al-Infiṭār.
rows.anchor: he should read these two sūrahs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both sūrahs address rich, arrogant Quraysh who ignored the warnings because they trusted their castles and edifices.
rows.anchor: The real addressees of both sūrahs are the rich and arrogant among the Quraysh who were turning a deaf ear to the warnings of the Qur’ ān just because they thought that no one would be able to break into their castles and edifices.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Takwīr reasons from the Qur’an’s authenticity, source, revelation, and bearer; its rejecters cannot distinguish radiant dawn from murky night.
rows.anchor: the bearer are all pure and upright.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Infiṭār instead reasons from God’s creativity, power, wisdom, justice, and mercy: signs of power and mercy in humans entail a coming day of reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: attributes of creativity, power, wisdom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is no difficulty for God: if first creation was easy, creating again is no harder, and the coming day is certain.
rows.anchor: creating again be difficult for Him?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s present respite for criminals gives them time to reform; those who refuse have no excuse or justification at Judgment.
rows.anchor: no excuse for their denial

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine delay does not mean words and deeds are hidden: angels have been assigned to everyone to record everything.
rows.anchor: This delay from God should not mislead people to think that their words or deeds are hidden from Him. He has deputed His angels on every person who are noting down each and everything.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 1–5 portray the heavens, stars, earth, and graves’ upheaval at Judgment and warn that every secret will be exposed.
rows.anchor: each and every secret will be revealed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human formation displays divine power, wisdom, mercy, and justice, showing that Judgment is possible and that human existence has purpose.
rows.anchor: With reference to the grandeur of divine attributes of power, wisdom, mercy and justice found in the formation of a human being a reminder is sounded that no one should think that the Day of Judgement is beyond the power of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s appointed angels carefully and faithfully record every word and deed, so people should not think he is unaware.
rows.anchor: He has deputed angels on each person who record all their words and deeds with full caution and faithfulness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous enter gardens of blessing, while wrongdoers enter Hell and never leave.
rows.anchor: Once they enter it, they will never

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment delivers impartial justice; all authority belongs to God and no one can intervene in another person’s affairs.
rows.anchor: A mention of the impartial justice which will be delivered on the Day of Judgement: on that Day, all authority and power will rest with God. No person will be able to interfere in someone else’s affairs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun iftiṭār means to be torn apart or rent asunder; the sky’s rupture at Judgment is also described with synonyms elsewhere.
rows.anchor: It is mentioned in the Qur’ ān at a number of places that

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next world begins under new physical laws as this world is destroyed; the exact destruction cannot be imagined, but the upheaval warns rich arrogant people who trust their buildings.
rows.anchor: The next world will come into existence under a new set

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent roof of the world will be shattered and fissured, so even man-made structures cannot protect the arrogant.
rows.anchor: the roof of this whole world will be shattered

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers should not speculate whether the sky is vacuum or solid matter; they should trust that its apparently flawless roof will be torn with fissures.
rows.anchor: this sky is a vacuum or solid matter;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intithār means scattering or dispersal; stars that now seem suspended like lamps on an invisible thread will fall and scatter when that thread is pulled away.
rows.anchor: Today the stars appear to be woven in an invisible string

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Takwīr says the stars lose light when the sun is destroyed and their solar-system relation ends; al-Infiṭār says they scatter because their supporting heavenly roof disappears.
rows.anchor: the very roof from which
